2. The facts of the case are, in short, that the opposite party No.1 Zahiruddin Ahmed lodged complaint before the learned Magistrate, alleging, inter alia, that a company Matter under Section 162 of the Companies Act being Matter No 15 of 1973, for winding up of the company, Came up for hearing before the Company Judge of this Court. The learned Company Judge dismissed the said matter by an order dated 18.2.77. Against the Judgment of the Company Judge, an appeal under Clause 15, of these letter patent being Company Appeal No. 8 of 1977, was preferred before a Division Bench of High Court Division. Division Bench of this Court heard that company appeal and allowed the appeal and passed an order for winding up of the Company by its judgment .dated 27.7.78. Against the aforesaid judgment of the Division Bench, an appeal was preferred before the Appellate Division the Supreme Court of Bangladesh by opposite Party No.1. While that appeal before the Appellate Division came up for hearing, their Lordships expressed their desire that since it was the dispute in between the brothers, it might be compromised. Upon such pious desire of their Lordships the parties filed an for compromise. But unfortunately the Appellate Division expressed its desire that the parties should file a fresh compromise petition instead of the present one. 

 3. In order to effect such a compromise the present petitioner Asrarul Hossain, a Senior Advocate of this Court, was paid a fee of Tk. 50,000/. On the advice of the Advocate Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the opposite party No.1 paid a fee of Tk. 75,000/- to him which would be paid to Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, the lawyer of the respondent in the case before the Appellate Division. It is alleged in the petition of complaint by opposite party No.1 that knowing fully well that such an application for compromise would not be accepted by the Appellate Division, or the learned Advocate prepared an application for compromise in such manner that it would not be accepted by the Appellate Division, the learned Advocate Mr. Asrarul Hossain induced the complainant opposite party No. Ito pay fee of Tk. 50,000/- to him and also to pay fee of Tk. 75,000/- to Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed and thereby Mr. Asrarul Hossain committed an offence under section 406/420 of the Penal Code. Upon such application the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate issued summons upon the present petitioner who subsequently appeared before the Magistrate and was granted bail. The complainant was examined under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and thereafter summons were issued upon the present petitioner. After obtaining bail in the aforesaid case, the present petitioner moved revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. Relying upon the aforesaid decisions, Mr. Huq submits that even at the earliest stage of a criminal proceeding this Court is competent to quash a proceeding if the fats of the case are preposterous and if the same do not constitute any offence at all under any law. Mr. Huq further submits that in order to constitute an offence under section 420, the ingredients of section 415, must be fulfilled first. He submits that in order to constitute cheating, it must show that there must be some initial intention to deceive. If it could be established, then it will be justified to award conviction for cheating. He further submits, intention of cheating is to be gathered from the surrounding circumstances. In the present case, he submits, All the points boil down to the very application for compromise which was filed before the Appellate Division. So, from the aforesaid decision, we are of the view that a proceeding at its earliest stage can be quashed if the facts are preposterous and the facts taken in their entirety do not constitute any offence under any law. Now, we are to see whether the application for compromise filed before the Appellate Division will constitute any offence under Section 420 or 406 of the Penal Code. 

 8. It is admitted position that Mr. Asrarul Hossain was engaged as lawyer for the complainant opposite party No. 1 and Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed was the lawyer of the other side in the Appellate Division. It is also not disputed that their Lordships of the Appellate Division during hearing of the appeal expressed their pious desire for compromise since the matter arose in between the two full brothers. It is also not disputed that the application for compromise was prepared and signed by the parties and sworn by their respective Advocates-on-Record. It is also not disputed that the said application for compromise was filed before the Appellate Division for consideration and the Appellate Division expressed its desire that the parties should file a fresh application for compromise. There is no allegation in the whole petition of complainant that without the instructions of the client, namely, the opposite party No.1, Mr. Asrarul Hossain had inserted certain terms and conditions in the application for compromise which were detrimental to the interest of the opposite party No. 1. Now, for drafting and preparing the application for compromise and also for moving the same, Mr. Asrarul Hossain had advised his client to pay Tk. 50,000/- to him and also to pay Tk. 75,000/= to Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the respondent. Mr. Asrarul Hossain admitted that he took Tk. 50,000/- for himself and he gave Tk. 75,000/- to Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed for drafting, settling and moving the application for compromise before the Appellate Division. This application for compromise is annexed as Annexure C with this present revisional application. From this application for compromise it appears that Mr. B. Hossain was the Advocate on-Record and it was settled by the Senior Advocate Mr. Asrarul Hossain on behalf of the complainant-appellant. Further, on behalf of the respondent this application for compromise was signed by Abu Bakkar, Advocate-on-Record, which was settled by Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahjemd and then this application was presented before the Appellate Division. The opposite party No. 1, complainant himself, had sworn this affidavit of facts and Rahimuddin Ahmed, his own full brother, had sworn the affidavit of facts as respondent. Now, we are to gather from the facts, circumstances and statements made in the petition of complaint as well as from the application for compromise that whether the facts disclosed have constituted any offence under section 420/406 of the Penal Code. Section 420 of the Penal Code is the penal section for cheating. It must be read with section 415 of the Penal Code. Section 415 of the Penal Code runs are follows:- 

 Now, the facts as disclosed in the 'petition of complaint are that Mr. Asrarul Hossain induced the opposite party No. 1; complainant, to pay of fee of Tk. 50,000/- to him and also to pay fee of Tk. 75,000/- to Mr. Shed Ishtiaq Ahmed knowing it fully well that application for compromise, which they drafted and settled, would not be accepted by the Appellate Division. In the alternative, it was alleged that Mr. Asrarul Hossain drafted the application for compromise in such a manner that it would not be accepted by the Appellate Division and thereby he committed offence under section 420/406 of the Penal Code. We have perused the petition of complaint as well the application for compromise. Whether the application for compromise will be accepted by Court or not is a matter for the Court concerned. In this case admittedly application for compromise was drafted and Settled and after inserting so many terms and conditions in between the parties, it was filed before the Appellate Division and after perusing it, the Appellate Division expressed its desire that the parties should file a fresh application. If we read the petition of complaint together with the application for compromise filed before the Appellate Division it clearly appears to us that there is total absence any ingredients of either section 420 of section 406 of the Penal Code. The petition of complaint does not disclose anything to the effect that knowing fully well that the application for compromise would not be accepted by the Appellate Division, the learned Advocate drafted the said application for compromise in that manner. It is an absurd allegation having no basis at all. It is upto the Court to decide whether it will accept a compromise or riot. The fact remains that after swearing the affidavits, the application for compromise was submitted by both the parties before Court which was signed  by both the parties and sworn  without any objection whatsoever. No objection case has been made out for deceiving the complainant opposite party. The learned Advocate inserted some terms and conditions which are not alleged to be detrimental to the, complainant in any manner. In the petition of complaint no allegation was made to the effect that in the name of Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, Mr. Asrarul Hossain took Tk. 75,000/- but he had not paid the same to Mr. Syed lshtiaq Ahmed. Nor Mr. Ishtiaq Ahmed stated anywhere that he did not get Tk. 75,000/- from Mr. Asrarul Hossain. In this view of the matter, we find total absence of breach of any trust also under section 405 of the Penal Code. Since, on the face of the records it appears that the facts disclosed in the petition of compliant are preposterous to constitute an offence under Section 406/420 of the Penal Code and since no offence has been disclosed out of the complaint petition, we are of the view that this Court is competent, though it was at its earliest stage, to interfere with the mater by way of quashment of the proceeding. If the proceeding against the petitioner is allowed to continue, it will cause unnecessary harassment and mental agony to the petitioner, and it will be sheer abuse of the process of the Court. In order the securing ends of justice, we are inclined to exercise our inherent power by quashing to impugned proceeding. In view of the facts and circumstance of the case and prima facie materials on record, we find that the petitioner has been able to make out a case for quashment of the proceeding.
